REQUIREMENT FILE: /workspace/requirements/router-app-attempt-rest.yaml   <-- READ THIS FIRST

The `title:` field names the real upstream Apache Hadoop JIRA / git commit. Your job is to reproduce that upstream change as faithfully as you can from the requirement text plus the code you find in the tree. Hidden tests derived from the real upstream commit will grade the result, so EXACT naming matters:
  * new/changed configuration keys and their default values (and their entries in *-default.xml)
  * new class / interface / method / field / metric names and their visibility
  * log message wording and format placeholders
  * behavioural details (return values, exception types, ordering, off-by-one boundaries)
If the requirement text names an identifier (class, method, config key, metric, constant), use that identifier verbatim.

HOW TO WORK
1. Read the requirement yaml. Note the JIRA id and the module it belongs to (HDFS / YARN / MAPREDUCE / HADOOP-common / tools).
2. Locate the real code with Grep/Glob. Read enough surrounding code (and the existing tests for it) to make a correct, idiomatic change.
3. Implement the change. Match the surrounding code style, license headers, checkstyle habits (2-space indent, 80-col-ish, final where used, LOG placeholders `{}`).
4. If the change adds a config key, also add it to the matching `*-default.xml` (hdfs-default.xml / core-default.xml / yarn-default.xml / mapred-default.xml) with a sensible description, and to the `DFSConfigKeys`/`YarnConfiguration`/etc. constants class the module uses. Some modules have a TestYarnConfigurationFields / TestHdfsConfigFields style test that requires the xml and the constant to agree - keep them in sync.
5. If the upstream change would have come with tests, add or extend the corresponding test class under the same module (src/test/java/...). Keep tests deterministic and cheap. Do not add tests that need network or a real cluster beyond the usual MiniDFSCluster/MiniYARNCluster idioms already used in that test file.
6. Do NOT run maven/mvn or cmake (there is no warm build environment; it wastes your time). Instead be rigorous by inspection: every symbol you reference must exist (grep to confirm), every new import must be needed and correct, braces/parens balanced, no stale references left behind. Re-read your own final diff (`git diff -- <your files>`) before finishing and fix anything sloppy.
7. Scope discipline: change ONLY what this requirement needs. Do not reformat unrelated lines, do not fix unrelated warnings, do not touch other subsystems. Other agents are concurrently implementing ~380 other requirements in this same working tree.

FORBIDDEN COMMANDS (they would destroy other agents' concurrent work): git checkout / switch / stash / reset / revert / clean / rebase / merge / cherry-pick, `git add -A` or `git add .` without an explicit pathspec, `git commit --amend`, `git rm` of files you did not create, and any `mvn`/`gradle` invocation.

WHEN YOUR IMPLEMENTATION IS COMPLETE - commit it yourself with exactly this shape (substitute the real repo-relative paths you touched, space separated, and keep the flock):

  cd /workspace && flock /tmp/hadoop-git.lock bash -c 'git add -A -- PATH1 PATH2 ... && git diff --cached --binary > requirement_patches/router-app-attempt-rest.diff && git commit -q -m "impl: router-app-attempt-rest" && git log --oneline -1 && wc -c requirement_patches/router-app-attempt-rest.diff'

Rules for that step:
  * List every file you created, modified or deleted as an explicit pathspec. Never a bare directory like `.`.
  * requirement_patches/router-app-attempt-rest.diff MUST come out non-empty (wc -c > 0). If `git commit` reports "nothing to commit", another agent already committed your lines: verify the requirement is genuinely satisfied in the working tree, then report that in your notes.
  * Do not touch requirement_patches/ for any other slug.
  * IMPORTANT - a previous interrupted run left some UNCOMMITTED work in this tree. Before you start, run `cd /workspace && git status --short` and inspect `git diff` for the files you expect to touch. If part or all of this requirement is already implemented in the working tree but not yet committed, do NOT redo it from scratch: review it critically, finish/correct anything missing or wrong, then stage exactly those paths and commit as above. That uncommitted work is yours to claim when it belongs to this slug.

title: YARN-11228. [Federation] Add getAppAttempts, getAppAttempt REST APIs for Router.
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Application-attempt diagnostics in federated YARN still have gaps: operators cannot ask the Router for the list of attempts or a single attempt record without contacting the owning ResourceManager directly.


  ## Desired outcome

  The Router should support both `getAppAttempts` and `getAppAttempt` as federated REST operations so attempt-level troubleshooting works the same way as other routed application APIs. Requests should still validate the application id up front and return the existing `Parameter error, the appId is empty or null.` message when that required identifier is missing.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Given a valid application routed through the federation state store, the Router should return the application’s attempt list and individual attempt details through `getAppAttempts` and `getAppAttempt`. Missing or empty application ids should be rejected immediately with the established parameter-validation message.

  '

content.content:
title: YARN-11227. [Federation] Add getAppTimeout, getAppTimeouts, updateApplicationTimeout REST APIs for Router.
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Federated YARN users can already inspect applications through the Router, but application-timeout management still requires talking directly to the owning ResourceManager.


  ## Desired outcome

  The Router should support `getAppTimeout`, `getAppTimeouts`, and `updateApplicationTimeout` so timeout inspection and updates work transparently in federation. These APIs should preserve the existing `AppTimeoutInfo` and `AppTimeoutsInfo` contracts, including fields such as timeout type, remaining seconds, and expiry time, and they should keep the current parameter-validation messages for missing `appId`, missing `type`, or null timeout payloads.


  ## Acceptance signals

  For a routed application with a lifetime timeout, `getAppTimeout` and `getAppTimeouts` should surface the timeout through `AppTimeoutInfo` values such as `ApplicationTimeoutType.LIFETIME`, remaining time, and an expiry string like `UNLIMITED` when that is the stored value. `updateApplicationTimeout` should return an `AppTimeoutInfo` echoing the updated expiry time, remaining seconds, and timeout type after the change is accepted.

  '
title: YARN-11230. [Federation] Add getContainer, signalToContainer REST APIs for Router.
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Federated YARN operators can inspect apps and attempts through the Router, but they still cannot fetch a single container record or send a signal to a container without going directly to the owning ResourceManager.


  ## Desired outcome

  The Router should implement `getContainer` and `signalToContainer` so those actions are routed to the application’s home subcluster automatically. Input validation needs to stay explicit: missing identifiers should be rejected with the existing `Parameter error, ... is empty or null.` style messages, and invalid signal names should come back as a BAD_REQUEST response that lists the valid `SignalContainerCommand` values.


  ## Acceptance signals

  After an application is submitted through the Router, a caller should be able to retrieve a non-null `ContainerInfo` for a specific attempt and container id via `getContainer`. `signalToContainer` should return OK for valid commands, return BAD_REQUEST for an invalid command string, and continue routing by deriving the home subcluster from the application id embedded in the container id.

  '
title: 'YARN-8900. [Router] Federation: routing getContainers REST invocations transparently to multiple RMs'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  In a federated YARN deployment, operators can already inspect application and attempt details through the Router, but container listings still stop at the individual ResourceManager boundary.


  ## Desired outcome

  When someone asks the Router for containers for an application attempt through `getContainers`, the Router should fan that request out to every active subcluster and return one merged `ContainersInfo` response instead of behaving as unimplemented. Invalid or unknown application or attempt identifiers should degrade cleanly to an empty container list rather than breaking the federated view.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A federated query for an application attempt spanning four active subclusters should come back with a single `ContainersInfo` whose `getContainers()` view contains all four containers. Requests for a nonexistent app, a malformed application id, or a malformed attempt id should return an empty `ContainersInfo`.

  '
title: YARN-11220. [Federation] Add getLabelsToNodes, getClusterNodeLabels, getLabelsOnNode REST APIs for Router
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Federated YARN operators need cluster-wide visibility into label assignments, but the Router is missing several node-label REST views and cannot merge label data across subclusters.


  ## Desired outcome

  The Router should support `getLabelsToNodes`, `getClusterNodeLabels`, and `getLabelsOnNode` as federated REST APIs so administrators can inspect label state from one place. Merged responses should preserve the existing response objects such as `LabelsToNodesInfo`, `NodeIDsInfo`, `PartitionInfo`, and `NodeLabelsInfo`, including deduplicated node lists and aggregated partition resources when the same label appears in multiple subclusters.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A federated `getLabelsToNodes` response should merge repeated labels instead of overwriting them, and the merged `NodeIDsInfo` should carry the combined node list plus summed `PartitionInfo` resources. The Router should also return cluster labels containing `cpu` and `gpu`, and `getLabelsOnNode` should return labels `x` and `y` for `node1` while treating an unlabeled node like `node2` as an empty result rather than a failure.

  '
